analysis:
All changed files in this batch are test-only: StatusResidencyTests.swift (adds retryingSelectedModelAndPendingFilterChange and switchedFilterAndLaterEdit), AutopilotPlacementFixture.swift (adds two test-only setters, setAutopilotResidentSinceForTesting and setAutopilotLeaseForTesting, at head lines 120-126), and three new test files for selected-model recovery and placement policy. No production sources are modified, so there is no new runtime attack surface, change to attestation, encryption, or cache-storage behavior (T-041), coordinator wire contract (TB-002), or provider key handling.

The tests do describe production behavior that this PR presumably introduces elsewhere. That behavior is not in this batch, so the next pass should check the production code. Selected-model recovery can evict idle models and can release an adopted Autopilot model after its hold expires, even while it has traffic in flight. SelectedModelPlacementPolicyTests asserts that a released model stops taking new requests and is advertised as withdrawn, and that a hold is always honoured. This touches availability (A-018) and the T-059 add-on hold interplay. anAddonHoldCancelsTheAttemptInProgress asserts that a recovery load is cancelled under an add-on hold. It uses the production hold API holdForAddon/endAddonHold, which these tests only exercise.

The fixtures use temporary directories under FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory for the daemon state file and write only synthetic model IDs and hashes. No secrets, prompts, or real keys appear. Test-only setters in a test-target extension via @testable import do not widen the production API.

Open question for integration, not a finding: the production recovery, eviction, and release logic (checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue, the adoption release) is outside the supplied evidence. Its handling of in-flight requests and its interaction with the add-on hold lease should be reviewed there.
